lessons.title: From Dial Square to Arsenal
lessons.subtitle: Woolwich beginnings and a north London home

story.title: An industrial beginning
story.body: Arsenal began in 1886 with workers from the Woolwich Armaments factory, forming a football community in south-east London.

story.title: A move that reshaped the club
story.body: After financial trouble and relegation, the club moved to Highbury in 1913. Its first match there was a 2–1 win over Leicester Fosse.

facts.label: Early team name
facts.prompt: What name was used for the unnamed Woolwich side when it played its first match?
facts.scope: The Woolwich team’s first match in December 1886, before the founding members chose the name Royal Arsenal
facts.evidence: Arsenal’s history says the unnamed team was referred to as Dial Square for its first match; it adopted Royal Arsenal at a meeting later that month.

facts.label: Founding community
facts.prompt: Which workers established the club?
answers: workers from the Woolwich Armaments factory
facts.scope: Arsenal’s 1886 origins in Woolwich
facts.evidence: The club overview attributes its founding to munitions workers at the Woolwich Armaments factory.

facts.label: First Highbury opponent
facts.prompt: Which team did Arsenal face in its first match at Highbury?
facts.scope: Arsenal’s first Highbury match, 6 September 1913
facts.evidence: Arsenal’s history says its first Highbury game was against Leicester Fosse on 6 September 1913.

lessons.title: The first Double
lessons.subtitle: A league title followed by an FA Cup final

story.title: A title in enemy territory
story.body: Arsenal clinched the 1970/71 league title at White Hart Lane, beating Tottenham 1–0 through Ray Kennedy.

story.title: A second trophy five days later
story.body: The club completed its first league-and-FA Cup Double by beating Liverpool 2–1 at Wembley.

facts.label: Title-clinching year
facts.prompt: In which year did Arsenal clinch the league title at White Hart Lane?
facts.scope: Arsenal’s 1970/71 league title
facts.evidence: Arsenal’s official history dates the title-clinching win at Spurs to 1971.

facts.label: Title-clinching scorer
facts.prompt: Who scored Arsenal’s title-clinching goal at White Hart Lane?
facts.scope: Arsenal’s 1–0 title-clinching win at Tottenham in 1971
facts.evidence: Arsenal’s official history names Ray Kennedy as the scorer.

facts.label: First Double final opponent
facts.prompt: Which team did Arsenal beat in the 1971 FA Cup final to complete its first Double?
facts.scope: Arsenal’s first league-and-FA Cup Double in 1971
facts.evidence: Arsenal’s history records a 2–1 FA Cup final win over Liverpool on 8 May 1971.

lessons.title: Anfield, 26 May 1989
lessons.subtitle: A late goal decided the title on the final night

story.title: The final-day equation
story.body: Arsenal needed a two-goal win at Liverpool to take the league title. Alan Smith scored after a free kick, then Michael Thomas broke through in injury time.

story.title: A last-second finish
story.body: The 2–0 result delivered the championship to Arsenal at Anfield, a defining away victory in the club’s history.

facts.label: Title-winning year
facts.prompt: In which year did Arsenal win the title at Anfield with a 2–0 victory?
facts.scope: Arsenal’s final-day title win at Liverpool
facts.evidence: Arsenal’s account identifies the match as the 1988/89 season title clincher on 26 May 1989.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the score when Arsenal clinched the title at Anfield?
facts.scope: Liverpool v Arsenal, 26 May 1989
facts.evidence: Arsenal’s account gives the final score as Liverpool 0, Arsenal 2.

facts.label: Injury-time scorer
facts.prompt: Who scored Arsenal’s decisive injury-time goal?
facts.scope: Arsenal’s 1989 title-clinching match at Anfield
facts.evidence: Arsenal’s account credits Michael Thomas with the vital injury-time goal.

lessons.title: Henry’s Highbury hat-trick
lessons.subtitle: A response that restored Arsenal’s momentum

story.title: A difficult week
story.body: After cup defeats ended Arsenal’s treble hopes, Liverpool led 2–1 at Highbury in April 2004.

story.title: Henry turns the match
story.body: Henry scored three times as Arsenal won 4–2, including a solo goal after running from inside the Liverpool half.

facts.label: Match date
facts.prompt: On what date did Henry score a hat-trick against Liverpool at Highbury?
facts.scope: Arsenal v Liverpool, Premier League, 9 April 2004
facts.evidence: Arsenal’s goal feature dates the hat-trick to 9 April 2004.

facts.label: Henry’s goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Henry score in Arsenal’s 4–2 win over Liverpool?
facts.scope: Henry’s hat-trick in the 4–2 win over Liverpool
facts.evidence: Arsenal’s account explicitly says Henry scored a hat-trick in the 4–2 win.

facts.label: Match score
facts.prompt: What was the final score in Arsenal’s match against Liverpool?
facts.scope: Arsenal v Liverpool at Highbury, 9 April 2004
facts.evidence: Arsenal’s goal feature states the Gunners won 4–2.

lessons.title: Henry’s 30-goal season
lessons.subtitle: A scoring award across three straight campaigns

story.title: A landmark league season
story.body: Henry scored 30 Premier League goals in Arsenal’s unbeaten 2003/04 title season.

story.title: A sustained run
story.body: He won the Golden Boot in three consecutive seasons from 2003/04 through 2005/06, and four times in total.

facts.label: 2003/04 league goals
facts.prompt: How many Premier League goals did Henry score in 2003/04?
facts.scope: Thierry Henry’s Premier League scoring in 2003/04
facts.evidence: The Premier League season review lists Henry as top scorer with 30 goals.

facts.label: Consecutive Golden Boots
facts.prompt: How many consecutive Premier League Golden Boots did Henry win from 2003/04 through 2005/06?
facts.scope: Henry’s Premier League scoring awards, 2003/04–2005/06
facts.evidence: The Premier League account says Henry claimed three consecutive Golden Boots in 2003/04, 2004/05 and 2005/06.

facts.label: Career Golden Boots
facts.prompt: How many Premier League Golden Boots did Henry win in total?
facts.scope: Thierry Henry’s completed Premier League career
facts.evidence: The Premier League account says Henry topped the scoring charts in four seasons.

lessons.title: Bergkamp’s Newcastle finish
lessons.subtitle: A turn and finish chosen as a personal favourite

story.title: A goal remembered
story.body: Bergkamp selected his goal at Newcastle on 2 March 2002 among his favourite Arsenal goals.

story.title: Skill in a tight space
story.body: He described the finish as instinctive: he decided to go around the defender as the ball arrived, then scored.

facts.label: Match date
facts.prompt: On what date did Bergkamp score his famous goal at Newcastle?
facts.scope: Dennis Bergkamp’s goal at St James’ Park
facts.evidence: Bergkamp’s Arsenal feature dates his Newcastle goal to 2 March 2002.

facts.label: Opponent
facts.prompt: Against which club did Bergkamp score this goal?
facts.scope: Bergkamp’s selected Arsenal goal, March 2002
facts.evidence: The feature identifies the match as against Newcastle United.

facts.label: Venue
facts.prompt: At which stadium did Bergkamp score the goal?
facts.scope: Bergkamp’s selected Arsenal goal, 2 March 2002
facts.evidence: The Arsenal feature locates the goal at St James’ Park.

lessons.title: The Leicester hat-trick
lessons.subtitle: A third goal became Bergkamp’s favourite

story.title: A night in 1997
story.body: Bergkamp’s favourite Arsenal goal came in the third goal of his hat-trick against Leicester City on 27 August 1997.

story.title: A brilliant finish, a shared result
story.body: He recalled controlling the ball, flicking it around a defender and finishing. Arsenal drew the match.

facts.label: Match date
facts.prompt: On what date did Bergkamp score his hat-trick against Leicester City?
facts.scope: Dennis Bergkamp’s hat-trick for Arsenal against Leicester
facts.evidence: Bergkamp’s selected goals feature gives the date as 27 August 1997.

facts.label: Hat-trick total
facts.prompt: How many goals did Bergkamp score against Leicester that night?
facts.scope: Bergkamp’s 27 August 1997 match against Leicester
facts.evidence: Bergkamp describes the favourite as the third goal of his hat-trick.

facts.label: Match result
facts.prompt: What was the result of Arsenal’s match against Leicester?
facts.scope: Arsenal v Leicester City, 27 August 1997
facts.evidence: Bergkamp says his hat-trick ended in a draw.

lessons.title: Shankly’s rebuild
lessons.subtitle: Promotion and a first league crown

story.title: A team rebuilt
story.body: Bill Shankly transformed Liverpool after taking charge in 1959. The club won promotion from the Second Division in 1962.

story.title: A new level of success
story.body: Liverpool became league champions in 1964, then won the club’s first FA Cup in 1965.

facts.label: Shankly arrival
facts.prompt: In what year did Bill Shankly take charge of Liverpool?
facts.scope: Bill Shankly’s Liverpool tenure
facts.evidence: Liverpool’s history account sets Shankly’s arrival in 1959.

facts.label: Promotion year
facts.prompt: In what year did Liverpool win promotion from the Second Division under Shankly?
facts.scope: Liverpool promotion under Bill Shankly
facts.evidence: Liverpool’s account dates promotion to 1962.

facts.label: First FA Cup
facts.prompt: In what year did Liverpool win the FA Cup for the first time?
facts.scope: Liverpool’s first FA Cup win
facts.evidence: The official honours history identifies 1 May 1965 as Liverpool’s first FA Cup triumph.

lessons.title: A long-awaited FA Cup
lessons.subtitle: Shankly’s Liverpool beat Leeds at Wembley

story.title: A first final win
story.body: Liverpool had reached earlier finals without lifting the Cup. On 1 May 1965, the team finally won it, defeating Leeds United 2–1 after extra time.

story.title: The decisive header
story.body: Ian St John scored the winner in the 111th minute.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which team did Liverpool beat in the 1965 FA Cup final?
facts.scope: FA Cup final at Wembley, 1 May 1965
facts.evidence: Liverpool’s official history says the final was against Leeds United.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the final score in Liverpool’s first FA Cup win?
facts.scope: Liverpool v Leeds United, 1965 FA Cup final
facts.evidence: Liverpool’s official history records a 2–1 extra-time win.

facts.label: Winning scorer
facts.prompt: Who scored Liverpool’s winning goal in the 1965 FA Cup final?
facts.scope: The 111th minute of the 1965 FA Cup final
facts.evidence: The club history credits Ian St John with the 111th-minute winner.

lessons.title: Rome, 1984
lessons.subtitle: Liverpool won the European Cup on penalties at Roma’s home

story.title: A final at the opponent’s stadium
story.body: Liverpool met Roma at the Stadio Olimpico on 30 May 1984. The match finished 1–1 after extra time.

story.title: Penalties decide the trophy
story.body: Liverpool won the shoot-out 4–2. Ian Rush converted his penalty during the shoot-out, helping secure the club’s fourth European Cup.

facts.label: Final year
facts.prompt: In what year did Liverpool beat Roma in the European Cup final in Rome?
facts.scope: Liverpool v Roma, European Cup final at Stadio Olimpico
facts.evidence: Liverpool’s retrospective identifies the final as 30 May 1984.

facts.label: Shoot-out score
facts.prompt: What was Liverpool’s winning penalty shoot-out score against Roma?
facts.scope: Liverpool’s European Cup final shoot-out against Roma
facts.evidence: Liverpool’s account records a 4–2 shoot-out victory.

facts.label: Score after extra time
facts.prompt: What was the score after extra time in Liverpool’s 1984 European Cup final against Roma?
facts.scope: Liverpool v Roma, 1984 European Cup final, after 120 minutes and before penalties
facts.evidence: Liverpool states that the final was a 1–1 draw at the Stadio Olimpico and required penalties.

lessons.title: Gerrard’s Cup final
lessons.subtitle: A late equaliser kept Liverpool in the 2006 final

story.title: West Ham lead twice
story.body: Liverpool trailed West Ham 2–0 and later 3–2 in the 2006 FA Cup final at Cardiff’s Millennium Stadium.

story.title: A goal from distance
story.body: Gerrard scored from around 30 yards in added time to make it 3–3. Liverpool won the shoot-out and the trophy.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which team did Liverpool face in the 2006 FA Cup final?
facts.scope: Liverpool’s 2006 FA Cup final at Cardiff
facts.evidence: Liverpool’s account identifies West Ham United as the opponent.

facts.label: Added-time score
facts.prompt: What score did Gerrard’s added-time goal produce?
facts.scope: Steven Gerrard’s late equaliser in the 2006 FA Cup final
facts.evidence: The official Liverpool retrospective says the late goal made it 3–3.

facts.label: Goal distance
facts.prompt: From approximately how far out did Gerrard score the late equaliser?
facts.scope: Gerrard’s 2006 FA Cup final equaliser
facts.evidence: Liverpool describes Gerrard’s late equaliser as coming from 30 yards.

lessons.title: The 2001 cup treble
lessons.subtitle: Three cup competitions, including the UEFA Cup final

story.title: A remarkable season
story.body: Liverpool won the League Cup, FA Cup and UEFA Cup in 2001. Gerrard started all three finals.

story.title: A European final goal
story.body: He scored in the 5–4 UEFA Cup final win over Alavés, a match decided by a golden goal.

facts.label: Treble year
facts.prompt: In what year did Gerrard win Liverpool’s League Cup, FA Cup and UEFA Cup treble?
facts.scope: Liverpool’s three cup wins in the 2000/01 season
facts.evidence: Liverpool records all three cup wins as part of the 2001 trophy treble.

facts.label: UEFA Cup final opponent
facts.prompt: Which team did Liverpool beat in the 2001 UEFA Cup final?
facts.scope: Liverpool’s 2001 UEFA Cup final
facts.evidence: Liverpool’s official history names Spanish side Alavés as the final opponent.

facts.label: UEFA Cup final score
facts.prompt: What was the final score when Liverpool beat Alavés in 2001?
facts.scope: Liverpool v Alavés, 2001 UEFA Cup final
facts.evidence: Liverpool’s official match history records a 5–4 victory after a golden goal.

lessons.title: Rush in the Rome shoot-out
lessons.subtitle: A personal career peak in the 1984 European Cup final

story.title: The first season treble
story.body: Rush’s 1983/84 campaign ended with Liverpool winning the league, League Cup and European Cup.

story.title: A daunting kick
story.body: In Rome, Rush converted his penalty in the shoot-out against Roma. He later called that kick the pinnacle of his career.

facts.label: Final season
facts.prompt: In which season did Rush win the European Cup in Rome with Liverpool?
facts.scope: Ian Rush’s Liverpool treble season
facts.evidence: Liverpool identifies the 1983/84 season as the treble campaign and dates the final to May 1984.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which team did Liverpool beat in the 1984 European Cup final?
facts.scope: European Cup final in Rome, 30 May 1984
facts.evidence: Liverpool’s account identifies AS Roma as the opponent.

facts.label: Rush’s own description
facts.prompt: How did Rush later describe his converted penalty in the 1984 final?
facts.scope: Ian Rush’s own recollection of the 1984 final penalty
facts.evidence: Rush described converting the Rome shoot-out penalty as the pinnacle of his career in the Liverpool interview.

lessons.title: Rush’s 1983/84 scoring season
lessons.subtitle: A personal best across a trophy-winning campaign

story.title: An exceptional total
story.body: Rush scored 47 goals in all competitions for Liverpool in 1983/84, his personal best season with the club.

story.title: A season of silverware
story.body: He appeared 65 times as Liverpool won the league championship, League Cup and European Cup.

facts.label: Liverpool goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Rush score for Liverpool in all competitions in 1983/84?
facts.scope: Ian Rush’s 1983/84 Liverpool season
facts.evidence: Liverpool’s official player profile states 47 goals in that season.

facts.label: Season appearances
facts.prompt: How many appearances did Rush make for Liverpool in the 1983/84 season?
facts.scope: Ian Rush’s 1983/84 Liverpool season
facts.evidence: Liverpool’s appearance-makers retrospective says Rush featured 65 times in 1983/84.

facts.label: Team trophies
facts.prompt: How many major team trophies did Liverpool win in Rush’s 1983/84 season?
facts.scope: Liverpool’s league, League Cup and European Cup in 1983/84
facts.evidence: Liverpool lists the league championship, European Cup and League Cup among its honours for 1983/84.

lessons.title: A club formed in Barcelona
lessons.subtitle: Gamper’s invitation grew into a football club

story.title: An open invitation
story.body: In October 1899, Joan Gamper placed an announcement inviting people interested in football to help form a club.

story.title: The founding meeting
story.body: On 29 November 1899, Gamper and eleven other men met in Barcelona and founded Foot-ball Club Barcelona.

facts.label: Founding date
facts.prompt: On what date was FC Barcelona founded?
facts.scope: FC Barcelona’s founding meeting
facts.evidence: The official club account dates the founding meeting to 29 November 1899.

facts.label: Founder
facts.prompt: Which person called the founding meeting for FC Barcelona?
facts.scope: FC Barcelona’s foundation in 1899
facts.evidence: The club account identifies Joan Gamper as the founder who called the meeting.

facts.label: Other founding attendees
facts.prompt: How many men besides Gamper attended the founding meeting?
facts.scope: The founding meeting at the Solé Gymnasium, 29 November 1899
facts.evidence: The club’s account says Gamper met with eleven other men.

lessons.title: Les Corts: Barça’s first great home
lessons.subtitle: The opening of a landmark stadium marked a new stage of growth

story.title: A growing club needed room
story.body: In the 1920s, Barcelona’s growing support prompted the construction of Les Corts, the club’s first great stadium.

story.title: A landmark opening
story.body: Les Corts opened on 20 May 1922 with an initial capacity of 22,000. Later enlargements tripled that capacity to 60,000, making the ground a visible marker of the club’s growth.

facts.label: Opening date
facts.prompt: On what date did Les Corts stadium open?
facts.scope: FC Barcelona’s Les Corts stadium
facts.evidence: Barcelona’s history page gives the opening date as 20 May 1922.

facts.label: Initial capacity
facts.prompt: What was Les Corts’ initial capacity?
facts.scope: Les Corts at its opening in 1922
facts.evidence: Barcelona’s history page states its initial capacity was 22,000.

facts.label: Expanded capacity
facts.prompt: To about how many spectators did the later expansions increase Les Corts’ capacity?
facts.scope: Les Corts after successive expansions
facts.evidence: The club history says successive enlargements tripled capacity to 60,000.

lessons.title: Wembley, 1992
lessons.subtitle: Koeman’s free kick delivered Barça’s first European Cup

story.title: A final reaches extra time
story.body: Barcelona and Sampdoria were goalless after 90 minutes in the European Cup final at Wembley.

story.title: A historic breakthrough
story.body: Ronald Koeman scored in the 111th minute for a 1–0 win, giving Barcelona its first European Cup.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which team did Barcelona beat in the 1992 European Cup final?
facts.scope: European Cup final at Wembley, 20 May 1992
facts.evidence: Barcelona’s official history identifies Sampdoria as the opponent.

facts.label: Winning scorer
facts.prompt: Who scored the winning goal for Barcelona in the 1992 final?
facts.scope: Barcelona’s first European Cup final, 1992
facts.evidence: The club names Ronald Koeman as the scorer of the winning goal.

facts.label: Goal minute
facts.prompt: In which minute did Koeman score the winning goal?
facts.scope: Koeman’s extra-time goal in the 1992 European Cup final
facts.evidence: Barcelona records the goal in the 111th minute.

lessons.title: Messi’s 91-goal year
lessons.subtitle: A calendar-year record split between club and country

story.title: A world record
story.body: Messi scored 91 goals in calendar year 2012, surpassing Gerd Müller’s previous mark of 85.

story.title: Two teams, one calendar year
story.body: The total comprised 79 goals for Barcelona and 12 for Argentina; keep the Barça portion separate from the overall record.

facts.label: Calendar-year total
facts.prompt: How many goals did Messi score in calendar year 2012?
facts.scope: Lionel Messi’s goals for club and country in calendar year 2012
facts.evidence: Barcelona reports a 91-goal calendar-year total.

facts.label: Barcelona goals
facts.prompt: How many of Messi’s 2012 goals were for Barcelona?
facts.scope: Messi’s 2012 calendar-year goals for Barcelona
facts.evidence: The club report breaks the 91 total into 79 for Barça and 12 for Argentina.

facts.label: Argentina goals
facts.prompt: How many of Messi’s 2012 goals were for Argentina?
facts.scope: Messi’s 2012 calendar-year goals for Argentina
facts.evidence: The club report states he scored 12 goals for Argentina in the 91-goal year.

lessons.title: Five against Leverkusen
lessons.subtitle: Messi set a Champions League single-match scoring mark

story.title: A knockout-round rout
story.body: Barcelona beat Bayer Leverkusen 7–1 in the Champions League round of 16 second leg on 7 March 2012.

story.title: Five goals by one player
story.body: Messi scored five times, becoming the first player to score five goals in a single Champions League match.

facts.label: Match date
facts.prompt: On what date did Messi score five goals against Bayer Leverkusen?
facts.scope: Barcelona v Bayer Leverkusen, Champions League round of 16
facts.evidence: The official season report dates the second leg to 7 March 2012.

facts.label: Messi’s goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Messi score in the match against Leverkusen?
facts.scope: Messi’s record-setting match in the 2011/12 Champions League
facts.evidence: The season report records five Messi goals in the 7–1 second-leg win.

facts.label: Match score
facts.prompt: What was the score in Barcelona’s second leg against Leverkusen?
facts.scope: Barcelona v Bayer Leverkusen, 7 March 2012
facts.evidence: Barcelona’s season report records a 7–1 victory.

lessons.title: Xavi’s international era

story.body: Xavi was part of Spain’s European Championship-winning teams in 2008 and 2012.

facts.label: World Cup title
facts.prompt: In what year was Xavi part of Spain’s World Cup-winning team?
facts.scope: Xavi’s international honours with Spain
facts.evidence: Barcelona’s official Xavi profile identifies him as part of Spain’s 2010 World Cup-winning team.

facts.label: Second European title
facts.prompt: In what year did Xavi win the European Championship with Spain again?
facts.scope: Xavi’s international honours with Spain
facts.evidence: Barcelona’s official Xavi profile lists Spain’s European Championship win in 2012.

lessons.title: Xavi’s first-team debut
lessons.subtitle: A first appearance and first goal arrived together

story.title: From La Masia to the first team
story.body: After progressing through Barcelona’s youth teams, Xavi debuted for the first team in August 1998 against Mallorca.

story.title: An instant contribution
story.body: He scored in that Spanish Super Cup debut, beginning a 17-season first-team chapter at Barça.

facts.label: Debut month
facts.prompt: In which month and year did Xavi make his Barcelona first-team debut?
facts.scope: Xavi’s Barcelona first-team debut
facts.evidence: The official profile dates the debut to August 1998.

facts.label: Debut opponent
facts.prompt: Which team did Barcelona face in Xavi’s first-team debut?
facts.scope: Spanish Super Cup, August 1998

facts.label: Debut goal

facts.evidence: The club profile notes that Xavi scored at the beginning of his first season.
